text_blocks.snippet: A clothing store credit card is an example of revolving debt. This type of debt allows you to borrow money up to a certain limit, repay it, and then borrow again, making it distinct from installment debt which involves fixed payments over a set period.

list.title: Revolving Credit:
list.snippet: Clothing store credit cards, like regular credit cards, offer a revolving line of credit. This means you can make purchases, pay down the balance, and then borrow again up to your credit limit.

list.title: Not Installment Debt:
list.snippet: Unlike installment debt (like a car loan or mortgage), where you have a fixed payment schedule, revolving credit allows for more flexible payments, including minimum payments and the option to pay off the balance over time.
